capture_engagement.description: Whether the engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) of the email your code rendered are captured as analytics events of the recipient. Defaults to true. A project whose admin turned engagement capture off captures nothing, whatever the send says.

distinct_id.description: Distinct ID of the recipient's person. The send and its engagement events are recorded against that person. Defaults to the recipient's email address.

from.description: Sender of the email your code rendered, as `security@example.com` or `Example <security@example.com>`, on a verified domain of the project. Without it, the email goes out from the project's default sender, or from its only verified sender when it has no default.

html.description: HTML body of the email, exactly as the recipient should see it. Through this tool the whole request as JSON, html and text included, must stay under 1 MiB, and quotes and line breaks count twice. A larger email can't be sent here.

reply_to.description: Addresses replies to the email your code rendered go to.

subject.description: Subject of the email your code rendered.

template_key.description: Names an email whose content your code rendered, such as `order-shipped`, so its metrics, logs and status group under it. Letters, numbers, hyphens (-) and underscores (_) only. Send it with `subject` and `html` or `text`. PostHog sends the content as is and never stores it as a template.

text.description: Plain text body of the email. Without it, PostHog derives the text from html. Through this tool the whole request as JSON, html and text included, must stay under 1 MiB.
